svg.title: A surface-mount standoff: no paste in the footprint vs the maker's stencil
svg.desc: Drawn to scale except copper and mask thickness, after a maker's datasheet for an M3 surface-mount standoff 5 mm long, with the plated hole most boards use. Top: plan views of the footprint, a 7.4 mm round copper pad around a 4.4 mm plated hole. Left, marked wrong: no paste in the footprint, so the pad stays bare. Right, marked right: the maker's stencil, a ring of paste from 4.48 to 7.27 mm split into four segments by 0.8 mm webs. Bottom: cut-away side views after reflow. The standoff's 6 mm body sits on the pad and its 4.2 mm locating collar drops 1.4 mm into the hole; its M3 thread runs right through. Left: no solder, so the standoff sits loose on the pad. Right: solder under the body, a fillet from the body out to the pad's edge, and solder drawn down the plated hole round the collar.

g.text: ✓ Paste openings as the maker draws them
Drops 1.4 mm into the hole and centers the standoff
Some solder also drains down the hole
The standoff just sits on the pad
M3 thread, open at both ends
The screw comes up through the hole
Drawn to scale except copper and mask thickness. Steel and FR4 are shown cut.
The maker's stencil is a starting point: the assembler often prints more paste than this.
After a maker's datasheet: M3 standoff, 5 mm long, drawn with the plated hole most boards use.
